title: Sebastian and the Inheritance
premise: When insurance investigator Ulyana Underhill is called to verify the death of town founder Aldous Wren, she discovers his coffin is empty and the death certificate was signed by a doctor who died two years earlier. Her search leads her to Sebastian Wren, the founder's disinherited grandson who supposedly drowned as a boy — and who may be very much alive, hiding in plain sight as the cemetery's groundskeeper. As Ulyana digs into the inheritance that vanished with Aldous's 'death,' she realizes half the town conspired to fake it to protect their fortunes, and someone is now killing off the conspirators one by one. In the end Ulyana finds Sebastian alive but dying of the same poison meant for Aldous, exposes the conspiracy at the reading of the will, and must choose between turning in the one person who ever made her feel she belonged and the law that defines her.
about_author: Edmund Joubert is the pen name of a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine who spent eleven years investigating suspicious deaths before turning to fiction. His novels are known for their forensic precision and their melancholy affection for small towns that keep too many secrets.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paperwork
chapters.summary: Ulyana Underhill arrives in Grayhollow to close out a routine life-insurance claim on town founder Aldous Wren. Through her POV we see her photographic memory catalog every detail of the funeral home, including a signature she can't quite place. The beat is quiet unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Six Feet of Nothing
chapters.summary: At the court-ordered verification, the coffin is opened: empty except for a child's shoe. Ulyana's POV captures her shock breaking through detachment; the undertaker faints. Emotional beat: the moment routine becomes obsession.

chapters.title: A Doctor Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Ulyana traces the death certificate to Dr. Emmett Voss, whose own obituary ran two years prior. POV alternates briefly with Sheriff Dane Colter, who resents her intrusion. Beat: first evidence this is not fraud by one man but a machine.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Hands
chapters.summary: Ulyana notices the young cemetery groundskeeper has Aldous Wren's eyes and a burn scar matching family records. His name tag reads 'Sebastian.' Her POV bristles with recognition she can't yet prove. Beat: the mystery acquires a face.

chapters.title: What the Will Withheld
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Ulyana reads Aldous's will: everything left to a grandson, Sebastian, declared drowned at age nine. Flashback fragments surface in her memory of the drowning file. Beat: inheritance as motive and wound.

chapters.title: Grayhollow Welcomes You
chapters.summary: A town-history chapter told partly through Ulyana's interviews: the Wren mill built everything, employed everyone, and owned everyone's debts. Warmth on the surface, fear underneath. Beat: belonging as currency.

chapters.title: The First Retainer
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts lawyer Harlan Pike about the estate; he stonewalls, then that night receives an anonymous payment reminder. His POV shows guilt curdling into panic. Beat: the conspirators begin turning on each other.

chapters.title: Shoe Size Nine
chapters.summary: Ulyana matches the coffin's child's shoe to the drowning-era records — it belonged to Sebastian. She returns to the cemetery at dusk and watches the groundskeeper burn something in a barrel. Beat: hunter and quarry circling.

chapters.title: Conversations with the Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana visits Aldous's widow, Maren, who speaks in riddles about 'the price we all agreed to pay.' Her POV reveals grief layered over complicity. Beat: sympathy complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: The Drowning File
chapters.summary: Ulyana reconstructs the 1974 drowning from memory: no body recovered, a witness statement from a girl named Odette Vale who later left town. Beat: the past asserting its gravity.

chapters.title: Odette's Postcard
chapters.summary: Tracking Odette, Ulyana finds she mailed a postcard to Grayhollow last month — postmarked locally. Someone claiming to be Odette may already be here. Beat: the dead witness everyone swears is dead may be near.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Ulyana stakes out the cemetery; Sebastian catches her watching and instead of fleeing says, 'You should stop digging.' Charged, ambiguous exchange from both POVs. Beat: alliance or trap?

chapters.title: Harlan Falls
chapters.summary: Lawyer Harlan Pike is found dead in his office, staged as suicide, his copy of the will missing. Ulyana's photographic memory spots the forged knot. Beat: the conspiracy has begun cleaning house.

chapters.title: The Mill Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian slips Ulyana a page of the old mill ledger showing payments to six names — the conspirators' hush fund. His POV: he's been waiting twenty years for someone to look. Beat: reluctant partnership forms.

chapters.title: Sheriff's Warning
chapters.summary: Colter orders Ulyana out of town; she notes his boots match prints at the cemetery. His POV admits he's protecting something he can't name. Beat: authority revealed as suspect.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Maren tells Ulyana that Aldous didn't drown his grandson — he faked the boy's death to hide him from someone inside the family. She stops short of saying who. Beat: the inheritance was protection, not greed.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: Banker Corliss Finch, second name on the ledger, vanishes; his boat is found adrift. Town whispers that the founder walks again. Beat: superstition tightening around fact.

chapters.title: Photographs of Nothing
chapters.summary: Someone searches Ulyana's motel room; her memory reconstructs the intruder's gait — Colter's. She photographs her own documents as insurance. Beat: the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: Odette, Alive
chapters.summary: Ulyana finds Odette Vale living under another name at a coastal boarding house. Old and terrified, Odette confirms she saw who put Sebastian in the boat that night — and that the person is still in Grayhollow. Beat: the witness exists; time is short.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Odette explains the bargain: the town's elite helped fake Sebastian's death because exposing the truth would have unraveled the mill's financing and their own fortunes. Beat: theme crystallized — survival purchased with silence.

chapters.title: Broken Trust
chapters.summary: Ulyana shares Odette's location with Sebastian; within hours the boarding house burns. Odette survives but flees. Sebastian's POV: rage and the sick certainty that someone used him. Beat: betrayal fractures the alliance.

chapters.title: Colter's Debt
chapters.summary: Cornered, Colter confesses his role: he buried the drowning report as a young deputy because Aldous held his father's crimes over him. He gives Ulyana the original report's last page — torn away. Beat: complicity explained, not excused.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: The missing page named the sixth conspirator; Ulyana reconstructs it from a 1974 photograph of the file she once handled in a regional archive. The initials point somewhere impossible: M.W. Beat: revelation aimed at the heart.

chapters.title: Maren Wren
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Maren, who admits she orchestrated the fake drowning to save Sebastian from Aldous himself — the founder was going to kill the boy to void the will and keep the fortune. Beat: villain and protector in one body.

chapters.title: The Empty Grave Explained
chapters.summary: Maren reveals Aldous isn't dead either: he fled after the scheme collapsed, and the empty coffin was her message that the truth would out. But someone else has been using the legend to kill. Beat: the mystery refracts again.

chapters.title: Ledger Blood
chapters.summary: Third conspirator dies — the former mill foreman, poisoned like the others. Ulyana identifies the toxin: same rare compound used in the mill's old preservation vats. Beat: the killer has industrial access.

chapters.title: Sebastian's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sebastian offers to surrender his claim publicly if the killings stop, drafting a confession. Ulyana realizes whoever is killing wants the inheritance unclaimed — and Sebastian's death would accomplish it. Beat: love sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Harlan's successor convenes the will reading; the whole town attends. Ulyana attends armed with documents. Sebastian appears openly for the first time. Beat: gathering storm, public stage set.

chapters.title: Poison at the Table
chapters.summary: Sebastian collapses mid-reading — dosed through the ink of the confession he signed. Ulyana's memory traces the pen to the estate office. Beat: climax ignites; the killer is inside the room.

chapters.title: The Sixth Name
chapters.summary: As Sebastian fights the poison, Ulyana lays out the full chain before the town: the sixth conspirator is the estate's executor, Aldous's estranged brother Merritt Wren, who never forgave being cut from the will. Beat: accusation lands.

chapters.title: Merritt's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Merritt confesses with terrifying calm: he killed to reclaim what he believed stolen, and he faked Aldous's death years ago to seize control quietly. He draws a weapon. Beat: villain fully unveiled.

chapters.title: Graveyard Standoff
chapters.summary: Colter, redeeming himself, disarms Merritt in the cemetery where it began; Ulyana shields the dying Sebastian. Beat: violence brief, emotional cost heavy.

chapters.title: Antidote and Ambulance
chapters.summary: The mill's own antidote protocol saves Sebastian; Ulyana rides with him, holding his hand, her memory replaying every moment they shared. Beat: tenderness after terror.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana testifies across three days, her perfect recall dismantling the defense. Maren accepts her share of consequences with dignity. Beat: justice exacting its price from everyone.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Ulyana is offered a promotion for closing the case — contingent on omitting the town's collective complicity. She weighs the institution that raised her against the truth. Beat: the investigator faces her own inheritance.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Ulyana declines the promotion and resigns, mailing her full report anyway. Quiet chapter, her POV alone, walking Grayhollow's streets one last time. Beat: self-belonging chosen over institutional approval.

chapters.title: The Headstone
chapters.summary: Sebastian, recovering, carves a new stone for the empty grave: not Aldous's name, but Odette's lost decades and the truth itself. They visit together. Beat: mourning what survival stole.

chapters.title: An Inheritance Kept
chapters.summary: Sebastian donates the Wren fortune to the town as a trust, dissolving the debt-power that corrupted it. Maren, from prison, writes her approval. Beat: inheritance redeemed into belonging.

chapters.title: Two Tickets Out
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Ulyana and Sebastian leave Grayhollow together on the morning train, her memory finally holding something she chose rather than merely recorded. Final line echoes the empty coffin — some graves are best left holding only truth. Beat: resolution, open-hearted.
